name: calc
title: Calculator
description: Answers what you type as you type it: arithmetic, units, currencies, percentages, dates, time zones and durations, with variables of your own.
author: pal

settings.label: Precision
settings.description: Significant digits in a result; integers are never rounded, units and rates show at most 6.

settings.label: Locale
settings.description: How numbers and dates are written (en: 1,234.5; tr: 1.234,5; de: 1.234,5). Also how a typed number is read.

settings.label: Home currency
settings.description: What a bare amount (12 usd) converts to. Empty: the time zone's currency.

settings.label: Variables
settings.description: One line per variable, `name = value`, a value being anything calc reads: `salary_hour = 54 usd`, `rent = 42000 try`, `height = 183 cm`. A value may use other variables (`salary_day = salary_hour * 8`) and is written with a dot for decimals whatever the locale. A name is letters, digits and underscores, not a currency. Then `rent / salary_month`, `salary_year to eur`, `height to ft`; the row's subtitle says what each name stood for.

store.tagline: Sums, units, currencies, dates and time zones as you type
features: Arithmetic, percentages and number bases: `2^10`, `15% of 240`, `255 to hex`
Units as people type them: `5 km to miles`, `72 f to c`, `5 ft 3 in to cm`
30 currencies by code, symbol or name (`€12 to $`), rates updated daily
Dates and time zones: `next friday`, `days until 25 dec`, `3pm istanbul to new york`
A second answer in the other form: the reverse conversion, a fraction, hex, the ISO date

screenshots.caption: 12 usd to try at the ECB's rate, the reverse as the second row; the pane shows the rate, its inverse and where it comes from
A day count, with the weeks and months on the right
10:00 UTC in Tokyo, the full date there as the second row
What a result can do: copy, paste into the app in front, copy without formatting

actions.title: Paste result
actions.description: Into the app that was in front.

calc.title: Calculator
calc.description: Type an expression; the result is the row. At the root, sums, conversions, dates, times in other zones and unix times answer inline under a Calculator section; a query that is none of those gets an Ask Calculator fallback row.
